partners.mechanism_chain: MPO (HGNC:7546) —DECREASES→ Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) (CHEBI:21964); Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) (CHEBI:21964) —LEADS_TO→ Myeloperoxidase deficiency (MONDO:0009694); HBB (HGNC:4827) —DISRUPTS→ heme biosynthesis (GO:0006030); HBA1 (HGNC:4826) —DISRUPTS→ heme biosynthesis (GO:0006030); HBA2 (HGNC:4828) —DISRUPTS→ heme biosynthesis (GO:0006030); heme biosynthesis (GO:0006030) —PRODUCES→ Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) (CHEBI:21964); Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) (CHEBI:21964) —LEADS_TO→ Oxidative stress (HP:0012411); Oxidative stress (HP:0012411) —LEADS_TO→ Heinz body anemia (MONDO:0007705). #### 1. Heinz body anemia  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.415)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6798695)

**Proposed mechanism:** MPO (HGNC:7546) —DECREASES→ Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) (CHEBI:21964); Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) (CHEBI:21964) —LEADS_TO→ Myeloperoxidase deficiency (MONDO:0009694); HBB (HGNC:4827) —DISRUPTS→ heme biosynthesis (GO:0006030); HBA1 (HGNC:4826) —DISRUPTS→ heme biosynthesis (GO:0006030); HBA2 (HGNC:4828) —DISRUPTS→ heme biosynthesis (GO:0006030); heme biosynthesis (GO:0006030) —PRODUCES→ Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) (CHEBI:21964); Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) (CHEBI:21964) —LEADS_TO→ Oxidative stress (HP:0012411); Oxidative stress (HP:0012411) —LEADS_TO→ Heinz body anemia (MONDO:0007705). Loss-of-function mutations in MPO lead to an inability to neutralize ROS, contributing to oxidative stress and potentially myeloperoxidase deficiency phenotypes. Concurrently, mutations in HBB, HBA1, or HBA2 can disrupt heme biosynthesis, leading to unstable hemoglobin and increased susceptibility to oxidative damage, manifesting as Heinz body anemia. Both pathways converge on the common consequence of increased oxidative stress.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in MPO do not affect ROS levels or that mutations in HBB/HBA1/HBA2 do not lead to increased oxidative damage in erythrocytes. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a high-frequency pathogenic variant in MPO or HBB/HBA1/HBA2 associated with Heinz body anemia.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of oxidative stress in these distinct hematological disorders could lead to the development of therapies targeting ROS scavenging or stabilization of hemoglobin, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
